answer: A trust graph exposes Sybil swarms like a lantern revealing a river at night. Verified interactions form edges in an open graph; trust scores come from random walks starting at a few vetted seeds, republished each season. A genuine newcomer gathers links from many unrelated strangers, so its score climbs. A farm's identities link mostly to each other, a tight cluster the walk rarely reaches, so their scores stay low however many names they mint. Anyone can mirror the public computation and challenge a suspicious score; one operator cannot fake the scattered ties real trust requires.
